To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrated a 125 Gb/s, single-polarized, burst-mode, NFDM transmission system with a record-high data-rate and spectral-efficiency of 2 bits/symbol and 2.0 bits/s/Hz, respectively.

a high spectral efficiency and high data rate can be achieved in a practical NFDM system by transmitting multiple nonlinear subcarriers, each with a high order modulation, while precompensating for the channel-induced nonlinear phase shift in the nonlinear Fourier spectrum.

we have experimentally demonstrated a record high data rate of 1.25 Tbit/s and spectral efficiency of 2 bits/sHz in a single polarization NFDM transmission over 976km of standard singlemode fiber by transmitting and processing a total of 222 subcarriers simultaneously, each of which was carrying 32QAM modulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high speed optical transmission systems with high spectral efficiency and robustness against fiber nonlinearity.
the development of a novel approach for the high-speed transmission of nonlinearly multiplexed data signals in the optical domain.
the design of high speed NFDM transmitters and receivers and the investigation of the performance of NFDM transmissions in the presence of fiber nonlinearities and chromatic dispersion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work has experimentally demonstrated the feasibility of a 2.5 bits/s/Hz spectral efficiency in a 125 Gb/ NFDM transmission system over 976  km of standard single-mode fiber with EDFA amplification.
NFDM can be used for high-speed optical communications.
the nonlinear Fourier transform has been successfully demonstrated to be a promising technique for high-speed optical communications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be applied to other nonlinear transmission formats, such as nonlinear polarization division multiplexing, to increase the data rates of future optical networks.
the proposed precompensated NFDM transmission system can be a promising alternative to the existing high-speed transmission systems for future optical networks.

we experimentally demonstrated a practical approach for high-speed NFDM transmissions with high spectral efficiency by increasing the number and modulation format of the subcarriers together and applying a precompensation for the phase-shift induced by the transmission channel in the nonlinear Fourier spectrum domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by increasing the number and the data rate of each nonlinear subcarrier and by using a precompensation scheme, the data rate and spectral efficiency of the NFDM transmission can be significantly increased.
the proposed approach can be readily extended to higher data rates, which is of paramount importance for the practical implementation of NFDM systems.
the data rate of nonlinear frequency division multiplexed transmission systems can be increased significantly by the application of the precompensation technique in the nonlinear frequency domain.
